Project bootstrap template kit

These templates turn the modular project bootstrap protocol into copyable project-local artifacts. Use the smallest useful subset. A short investigation still receives the mandatory rollout packet; only the remaining templates are optional and should be selected when they add value.

Template Purpose
intake.md Paste into the new project's Slack thread or conversation to shape the project from a source thread.
project-profile.yaml Record the living project identity, surfaces, modules, team, controls, and unknowns.
rollout-packet.md Record the deployment profile, allowlists, dedicated Slack app/channel isolation, activation evidence, fallback, and rollback for every presented project.
provider-roles-contract.yaml Record the project-local eight responsibility areas and the Cursor, Antigravity, Perplexity, and OpenAI boundaries.
workstream-plan.md Split the current phase into bounded, non-conflicting assignments and select provider workflow skills.
review-ready.md Prompt a different eligible provider to review an exact candidate and carry it toward the configured merge gate.
project-state-report.md Report a bootstrap, reshaped plan, milestone, pause, or completion without implying unperformed actions.
minimal-fix.md Record one eligible low-cost mechanical correction and its focused proof.

Use

  1. Copy the template into the project-local channel, issue, document, or repository.
  2. Replace every angle-bracket placeholder that is material now.
  3. Delete optional sections that add no value.
  4. Label uncertain values provisional or unknown; do not invent them.
  5. Keep unconfirmed repositories, refs, spending, data access, and external actions analysis-only.
  6. Create rollout-packet.md for every project presented to the Director. Concurrently active deployments require a distinct Slack app, project channel, and profile/state namespace. Pending identities block Slack activation but not analysis-only shaping. Record secret references and readiness only—never token values. The rollout packet is mandatory; only the other bootstrap templates may be omitted.
  7. Select shared skills by catalog name only after the active session discovers them:
    • cursor-agent-workflow
    • antigravity-sandbox-workflow
    • perplexity-research-workflow
    • pplx-cli remains a Perplexity research-only terminal transport.
  8. Treat skill selection as procedure, not permission. The project profile, provider contract, and deterministic gates remain authoritative. Canonical provider roles: docs/team-operating-charter.html. Copy provider-roles-contract.yaml whenever you use project-profile.yaml, including single-provider projects. The profile always sets team.provider_roles_contract, so omitting the companion file leaves that reference dangling. It mirrors the charter and grants no authority of its own; a one-provider project simply records that provider's boundaries and leaves the rest unstaffed.
  9. Use the event vocabulary from project-bootstrap-protocol.md: PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP (intake record), BOOTSTRAP, PLAN, WORKING, EVIDENCE, REVIEW_READY, DECISION, OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED, RESHAPED, PAUSED, COMPLETE.
  10. Use minimal-fix.md only for the charter's up-to-three-attempt minimal-fix lane; changed candidates still require fresh exact-candidate evidence.
  11. Write no new in-file tags. Use Contributed-by: <Assistant or Tool> | <Complete Model or System> trailers on every commit and one Sole author: <assistant> (<model>) PR header, with assistance when applicable. Keep Co-Authored-By trailers. Follow the attribution policy and PR #284. Existing tags are historical pending mechanical cleanup.

Do not place secrets, credentials, tokens, raw private source, or unnecessary source-thread content in any template. Name Slack destinations only from the project profile or runtime configuration—never hardcode workspace channel names.
